To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the N170 is sensitive to stimulus physics, not to emotional meaning; and (2) the early posterior negativity (EPN) is sensitive to both stimulus physics and emotional meaning, while the late positive potential (LPP) is only sensitive to emotional meaning.
the processing of emotional meaning and stimulus physics are dissociable in the time frame of 100–200ms, but converge in later stages.
the P1 and the N170 are sensitive to the physical properties of the stimuli, whereas the EP components elicited by the emotional stimuli are modulated by the semantic content of the stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the time course of the processing of emotional stimuli and the interplay of stimulus physics and emotional semantics in this process.
the question of how emotional meaning is processed and how this processing is influenced by the visual properties of a stimulus.
the question how the brain processes different features of emotional pictures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the P1 component is sensitive to stimulus orientation whereas the N170 is not sensitive to emotional meaning but rather to stimulus orientation.
the P1 is sensitive to both stimulus meaning and orientation.
both the physical and the semantic aspects of a stimulus are important in determining the processing of emotional pictures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early processing of emotional stimuli is not exclusively determined by the physical characteristics of the stimulus.
the brain is sensitive to the emotional content of communicative gestures and that this sensitivity may be reflected in the P1.
the brain processes the physical properties and semantic content of emotional stimuli in parallel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N170 is a robust marker for visual stimulus orientation, but is insensitive to emotional meaning.
the processing of emotional pictures is not a unitary process but rather a complex sequence of different subprocesses, each of which may be modulated by different stimulus attributes.

the N170 is not sensitive to the emotional meaning of communicative hand gestures, and that the early posterior negativity component and late positive potential are more likely sensitive to emotional stimulus processing.
